About the Position

A self-funded PhD programme focusing on the built environment's contribution to GHG emissions and holistic carbon reduction strategies across the whole life cycle.

OpportunitySelf-Funded PhD: Sustainability and Carbon Management
HostHeriot-Watt University
LocationEdinburgh, United Kingdom
Study LevelPhD
FundingSelf Funded
StipendNo awarded stipend or tuition funding
Application DeadlineRolling
ApplyOfficial application page ↗

Funding detail: No awarded stipend or tuition funding; applicants must arrange their own support.

Basic Information

  • Host Institution: Heriot-Watt University, School of Energy, Geoscience, Infrastructure and Society
  • Study Level: PhD
  • Start Date: September
  • Funding Type: Self-funded
  • Tuition Fees (International): £20,456 per year
  • Location: Edinburgh
  • Official Website: https://www.hw.ac.uk/study/research/sustainability-carbon-management

Project Overview & Significance

This self-funded PhD programme offers a critical opportunity to address one of the most pressing global challenges: climate change and the sustainability of the built environment. The built environment is responsible for up to 50% of global CO2 emissions, making it a key target for decarbonisation efforts. This programme invites researchers to take a holistic view of carbon management, examining the entire life cycle of buildings and infrastructure—from the initial design concept through to demolition and material reuse. The research aims to identify innovative strategies for carbon reduction, promoting sustainable practices that can be adopted by the construction and energy sectors. By advancing knowledge in this field, graduates will contribute directly to global net-zero targets.

Research Themes & Objectives

Research within this programme can cover a wide range of topics, including carbon accounting, life cycle assessment (LCA), sustainable materials, green infrastructure, and energy-efficient building design. The objective is to develop new methodologies for measuring and reducing the carbon footprint of the built environment. Students might explore the integration of renewable energy technologies into building design, or policies that incentivise sustainable construction practices. The ultimate goal is to produce research that influences industry standards and government policy, fostering a transition towards a low-carbon built environment.

Training & Development

Students in the School of Energy, Geoscience, Infrastructure and Society benefit from access to advanced laboratories and computational resources. The school has strong ties to industry, providing opportunities for applied research and networking. Training includes research methods, academic writing, and subject-specific workshops. Graduates emerge with expertise highly sought after by engineering consultancies, government agencies, and sustainability NGOs.

Eligibility and Requirements

Applicants must hold a first-class or upper second-class honours degree in a relevant discipline, such as environmental engineering, civil engineering, or sustainability. As this is a self-funded programme, applicants must secure their own funding to cover tuition fees and living expenses. International students are welcome, with annual tuition fees set at £20,456.

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: Rolling - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.

About Heriot-Watt University

Heriot-Watt University is a public university with campuses in Scotland, Dubai and Malaysia. It offers undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral education in fields including engineering, computing, physical sciences, business and design. Its teaching and research emphasise practical applications, connecting expertise with industry and challenges in technology, sustainability and the wider economy.

Official website: https://www.hw.ac.uk/

How to Apply & Official Contacts

Prospective candidates should first develop a detailed research proposal and identify a potential supervisor within the School of Energy, Geoscience, Infrastructure and Society. Applications can be submitted via the Heriot-Watt University application portal. For general enquiries, contact study@hw.ac.uk. Detailed information on the programme and application guidelines can be found on the official university website.
